newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss to hand Mali cash deposited by dictator.
newsitem.headline: Swiss to hand Mali cash deposited by dictator.

text.p: Switzerland will return 3.2 million Swiss francs ($2.2 million) to Mali that the west African state's authorities say was stolen by ousted former dictator Moussa Traore, Swiss justice officials said on Thursday.

It will be the first time that Switzerland has handed over money from a toppled head of state based on claims by a successor government that the cash was put aside criminally, Berne's Federal Police Agency said.
"As far as cases of former heads of state go, it is the first time," agency spokesman Folco Galli said.
Galli confirmed a report in the Swiss news magazine Facts that the money would be repatriated soon, after a final ruling by the Swiss supreme court in March.

Legal wrangling has stalled efforts to return fortunes put in Swiss bank accounts by Philippines strongman Ferdinand Marcos, ousted in 1986, and by Haiti's Jean-Claude "Baby Doc" Duvalier, overthrown the same year.
Mali's new government asked Switzerland to freeze and return funds after the military ousted Traore in 1991 and paved the way for multi-party democracy.
"The money involved here came from embezzlement, corruption and other criminal acts," police spokesman Galli said.

The Federal Police Agency, which looks after Switzerland's response to requests for international legal aid, ordered the accounts frozen in September 1991 after the new Mali government pledged to offer a formal request, which followed in November.
